rv.q: Collette breathes an exuberance into the role — one that shows a different side of Beetlejuice, if even for a moment.
Beetlejuice (Justin Collette) mostly lurches back and forth along the schoolyard-bully-to-sad-sack-comedian pipeline.

sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at Marquis Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.
Farther from the stage than center orchestra — less up-close, but the sound still carries well.
At 1,611 seats, Marquis Theatre is one of the larger Broadway houses — far side mezzanine seats sit well off-axis and a long way from the stage.

vs.sum: The Marquis Theatre offers excellent comfort with spacious seating and good sightlines from most areas, although the ambiance is somewhat lacking due to its modern, hotel-integrated design. Facilities are well-equipped with ample restrooms and concessions, making it a convenient choice for theatergoers.

acc.note: Elevator via Marriott Marquis hotel. 10 wheelchair spaces. No elevator to Mezzanine.
